job.title: Coordinator Revenue Services
job.description:
Coordinator Revenue Services
Livingstone Shire Council | Yeppoon, QLD | QLGIA Level 6 | Starting at $109,779 + 13% super

Public Sector People are proud to partner with Livingstone Shire Council to recruit an experienced Coordinator Revenue Services.

This is an opportunity to step into a key leadership role within Council’s Financial Services team, overseeing the day-to-day operations of Revenue Services and leading a team of five.

Reporting to the Manager Financial Services, you will bring strong revenue and accounting expertise together with people leadership, stakeholder management and a continuous improvement mindset.

The role will play an important part in ensuring Council’s revenue operations are accurate, compliant and effective, while supporting the team through ongoing development, process improvement and knowledge sharing.

Relocation support is available for eligible candidates including up to $4,000 in relocation reimbursement and up to $2,000 in temporary accommodation support, subject to Council approval and conditions.

The Opportunity
As Coordinator Revenue Services, you will lead, develop and manage the Revenue team, ensuring high performance, operational effectiveness and a consistent approach to service delivery.

You will oversee Council’s revenue systems, rating structures and processes, while providing specialist advice across revenue, rates, fees and charges, debt recovery and related financial matters.

This is a hands-on leadership role where your ability to support and develop your team will be just as important as your technical revenue expertise.
Key responsibilities will include:
  • Leading, developing and managing the Revenue Services team to deliver high performance and continuous improvement
  • Overseeing revenue systems, rating structures and processes to ensure accurate billing, collection and legislative compliance
  • Providing expert revenue and financial advice to internal stakeholders and the community
  • Supporting the development and review of revenue policies, procedures and processes
  • Contributing to budgeting, financial reporting, strategic financial planning, audits, reconciliations and internal controls
  • Managing Council’s revenue accounts, fees and charges registers and associated processes
  • Identifying opportunities to improve revenue practices, systems and service delivery
  • Supporting effective resource management across the Revenue Services function
  • Building strong working relationships across Financial Services, Council and the broader community
  • Supporting the development of team capability, knowledge sharing and succession planning
  • Ensuring accurate records, sound governance and compliance with relevant legislation and Council policies
About You
You will be an experienced revenue or accounting professional who understands the complexities of revenue management and is confident leading a team in a local government or similar environment.

You’ll bring strong technical capability, but equally important will be your ability to lead people, build relationships and identify practical opportunities to improve the way revenue services are delivered.

You’ll bring:
  • Demonstrated experience in revenue accounting, rating legislation, debt recovery and/or related financial services
  • Strong understanding of rates, fees and charges and revenue processes
  • Proven people leadership and team management capability
  • Strong analytical, conceptual and problem-solving skills
  • The ability to interpret legislation, financial standards and Council policies and translate these into practical outcomes
  • Strong communication, consultation, negotiation and stakeholder management skills
  • Experience developing and improving policies, procedures and operational processes
  • Strong financial systems capability and sound organisational and time management skills
  • The ability to provide practical financial advice and work collaboratively across a range of stakeholders
  • A proactive approach to continuous improvement and team development
  • A strong commitment to professional and ethical conduct
You will also hold:
  • Tertiary qualifications in Business, Accounting or a related discipline
  • Substantial experience in a revenue management or accounting-focused position
  • Strong experience across financial and revenue management systems, with TechOne and Pathway experience highly regarded
  • A current C Class driver licence
Previous experience within a local government environment will be highly regarded, particularly experience across rates, revenue, recovery and property-related functions.

Why Livingstone Shire Council?
Livingstone Shire Council is located on Queensland’s Capricorn Coast, encompassing the communities of Yeppoon, Emu Park and surrounding rural areas.

This is an opportunity to join a regional Council and make a tangible contribution to the way revenue services are delivered to the local community.

The role offers:
  • Permanent, full-time employment
  • QLGIA Level 6 classification
  • Relocation support of up to $4,000, plus up to $2,000 temporary accommodation support, for eligible relocations
  • Competitive starting salary of $109,779 + 13% superannuation
  • A nine-day fortnight supporting a strong work-life balance
  • The opportunity to lead a five-person Revenue Services team
  • A role with genuine scope to improve systems, processes and team capability
  • The opportunity to contribute to broader Financial Services outcomes
  • A supportive regional lifestyle on the Capricorn Coast
This is an opportunity for an experienced revenue professional to take on a leadership role where you can make a genuine impact, both through the technical work you deliver and the team you lead.

If you are an experienced revenue or accounting professional looking for a leadership opportunity within local government, we would like to hear from you.

job.title: Automation Technician
job.description:
Industrial Automation Technologist / Technician

Location: Wetherill Park, Sydney
Industry: Advanced Manufacturing (Injection Moulding & Automation) Employment Type: Full-time, 24/7 manufacturing environment

About the Role
Our client, an established manufacturing operation based in Wetherill Park, is seeking an experienced Industrial Automation Technologist/Technician to join their team. This is a hands-on, technically diverse role supporting PLC-driven automation, industrial robotics, injection moulding machinery, and high-speed production equipment across a 24/7 site.

You'll be a key technical point of contact for production issues relating to equipment performance, product quality, and efficiency — working closely with Production, Maintenance, and Quality teams to minimise downtime and maximise OEE.
This role blends fault-finding, preventative maintenance, die setting, process optimisation, and continuous improvement, with genuine exposure to automation upgrades and manufacturing improvement projects.

Key Responsibilities
Automation & Technical Maintenance
  • Troubleshoot and maintain industrial automation and production equipment across a 24/7 environment
  • Service, repair, and set up injection moulding machines, industrial robots, IML systems, and auxiliary equipment
  • Fault-find and replace mechanical, electrical, hydraulic, and pneumatic components
  • Integrate industrial robots into material handling, inspection, and packaging applications, including safety interlock verification
  • Perform preventative and predictive maintenance, equipment upgrades, and calibrations
  • Complete major equipment overhauls and support complex machine, processing, and die-setting issues
Production & Process Support
  • Act as a key technical contact for production issues affecting output, quality, reliability, and efficiency
  • Perform die, insert, and colour changes, including machine start-ups and shutdowns
  • Set, adjust, and optimise robotics, machine software, and production process parameters
  • Troubleshoot production faults, including IML and high-speed packaging equipment
  • Maintain target cycle times while ensuring finished products meet specification
Continuous Improvement & Problem Solving
  • Investigate recurring and new faults using structured root-cause analysis; implement corrective and preventative actions
  • Analyse downtime, rejects, defects, and waste to identify improvement opportunities
  • Support automation design, programming, commissioning, and equipment upgrades
  • Maintain accurate records of downtime, rejects, NCRs, maintenance activities, and corrective actions
Quality & Compliance
  • Work closely with Quality Assurance to ensure equipment and processes meet product, customer, and regulatory requirements
  • Ensure compliance with site quality systems, HACCP, and applicable food safety requirements
  • Verify new or modified automation systems before production handover
Safety & Team Support
  • Work in line with WHS legislation, site safety procedures, and permit requirements
  • Identify, report, and rectify hazards and near misses
  • Coordinate with third-party service technicians when required
  • Support training and technical upskilling of production and maintenance personnel
  • Communicate and escalate technical issues across shifts to maintain operational continuity
About You
  • Proven experience in industrial automation, robotics, and/or injection moulding within a manufacturing environment
  • Strong mechanical, electrical, hydraulic, and pneumatic fault-finding skills
  • Experience with PLC-driven systems and industrial robot integration
  • Die-setting experience highly regarded
  • Comfortable working in a fast-paced, 24/7 production environment
  • Strong root-cause analysis and continuous improvement mindset
  • Food safety/HACCP exposure an advantage
  • Ability to train and support colleagues, and communicate effectively across shifts
Why Apply
  • Stable, full-time opportunity with genuine exposure to modern automation technology
  • Hands-on role combining automation, robotics, and process engineering — not a narrow, single-skill position
  • Real input into equipment upgrades and manufacturing improvement projects
  • Work within an established, well-resourced manufacturing operation
